summary: The public design selects a future modular platform monorepo with one trusted Host, PostgreSQL-backed .NET worker semantics and separate runners, after completed published/installed v2. Local generation/pure validation can run without the scheduler; unattended recovery uses the same database authority rather than a second SQLite workflow engine. Domain rules/authorization stay inward, Specifications/Planning perform no network I/O and the Host composes adapters. Proposed Forgejo owns its native repository/PR/check/delivery facts, while Specairn owns scheduling, operation journal and progress; the forge is outside the execution hot path. A separately qualified canonical Forgejo instance/version and protected PR/custody/restore journey are M1 obligations. The public GitHub reservation can be an asynchronous outward mirror with no independent write/delivery authority. Product runtime libraries remain independently buildable and generic FsQuint independently owned. No v2 API/state compatibility or historical-run import is selected; product adoption into fresh v3 workspaces is a distinct decision. This is proposed architecture, not an implemented Host, deployed forge, current migration or cutover authorization. Native empty-repository metadata is kept as a live audit observation outside this Git-cited architecture record.
title: Proposed Specairn Host and forge boundary
